---
title: "Teaching and Learning"
---

I teach because it changes how people think and sharpens my own understanding. In teaching, as in research, I aim to raise the floor, not only push the frontier. That means helping every student along, not just the brightest. Clarity and rigor are how I do it. I offer several ways into a hard idea, and I build materials that are computationally reproducible, so students can trace and change every result. Raising the floor also means making sure students from disadvantaged backgrounds know about and use campus resources such as tutoring and advising. I can teach methods for policy analysis, program evaluation, and applied econometrics, as well as most undergraduate courses in economics and statistics. I would especially like to teach a course on Open Policy Analysis.

## Teaching and Learning with AI

In mathematics, AI now generates proofs faster than mathematicians can digest them (Tao 2026). For teaching, the lesson is that producing gradable output is no longer the challenge. Understanding it is. "You can outsource your thinking, but you cannot outsource your understanding" (Karpathy 2026).

I use AI coding agents such as Claude Code every day. I built every course in the [Self-Directed Courses](#self-directed-courses) section below with them. The [refresher on machine learning](https://fhoces.github.io/ml-discrimination-refresher/), for example, took less than a week. Students who use these tools also need concepts once left to programmers, such as version control and verification plans, and I plan to teach them in the first classes.

I plan to assess what a student understands, not how finished the work looks. Verification comes first, and it is a module of its own in my [Administrative Data Pipelines](https://github.com/fhoces/admin-data-pipelines) course. I will give students AI-generated output with errors in one section and ask them to find them. Explanation is the test of understanding, through in-class tests and AI routines that question a student one step at a time. For disclosure of AI use, I lead by example, as in my [open policy analysis of the economic effects of AI](https://fhoces.github.io/opa-ai-macro-econ-scenarios/index.html#how-ai-was-used).

## Self-Directed Courses {#self-directed-courses}

I am also exploring private-sector positions in the Bay Area. To support this transition, I have been building a series of short, self-directed courses to refresh and develop skills relevant to the roles I'm targeting, such as policy researcher, applied policy economist, and data scientist positions at technology platforms.

The courses below were built using Claude Code. Each course is a set of xaringan slide decks with worked examples, R/Python/SQL exercises, and interview-style practice questions, all threaded through industry-related applications.

::: course-list
- [**ML Refresher: Discrimination and Fairness**](https://fhoces.github.io/ml-discrimination-refresher/). Bias-variance tradeoff, linear models, model evaluation, fairness frameworks, and the impossibility theorem. Every module pairs an ML concept with a discrimination scenario.
- [**Discrimination in Labor Economics Refresher**](https://fhoces.github.io/discrimination-econ-refresher/). Becker, Phelps, audit studies (Ge et al. 2016), Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition (Cook et al. 2021), algorithmic audits, and the practitioner playbook.
- [**Intro to Experiments in Industry**](https://fhoces.github.io/experimentation-refresher/). Potential outcomes and the experimental ideal, SUTVA and interference, cluster/switchback designs, regression adjustment and CUPED, ITT vs LATE, and external validity.
- [**Causal Inference Beyond A/B**](https://fhoces.github.io/causal-inference-beyond-ab/). Deep-dive course on causal inference for platform settings: modern DiD, synthetic control, causal forests, policy learning, and matrix completion.
- [**Intro to SQL**](https://fhoces.github.io/sql-industry-prep/). SELECT through window functions, drilled on a synthetic ride-sharing schema. Five modules of interview-style questions designed to be answerable from a cold start in under two minutes each. [One pager](https://fhoces.github.io/sql-industry-prep/sql-cheatsheet.pdf).
- [**Python for an R User**](https://fhoces.github.io/python-for-r-users/). The pandas + statsmodels stack, framed as a dplyr-to-pandas translation. Covers data wrangling, joins, OLS, A/B test inference, and difference-in-differences, with end-to-end interview scenarios.
:::
